messages.text: What kind of base on Franklin
Searched the catalog · Replogle Franklin 12 Antique Ocean Desk Globe

The Franklin has a sturdy base with a numbered semi-meridian, but the listing doesn't spell out the exact base material — just that it's durable and built to hold the globe steady. If you want something where the base material is specifically called out, the Cranbrook 12-inch Antique Desk Globe (which you also looked at) has a clearly stated walnut hardwood base. Want me to compare the two side by side?
Are all gloves based on national geographic maps

No — only the globes in our National Geographic collection (like the National Geographic Hudson or National Geographic Bartlett) use National Geographic's cartography. The rest, including the Franklin and Cranbrook you were looking at, use Replogle's own in-house maps. Both are accurate and regularly updated, just produced by different cartography teams. Were you drawn to the National Geographic name specifically, or just curious?
Are the national geographic more accurate, better print and more legible, better alignment at seams

I don't have specs comparing print quality, legibility, or seam alignment between the National Geographic line and Replogle's own globes — that detail isn't something I can confirm either way. Both lines are presented as accurate, detailed cartography, but for a print-quality comparison like that, I'd point you to (email hidden) so they can give you a straight answer. Is that the deciding factor between the Franklin and a National Geographic model for you?
